title: Derived invariants agree with two-term cohomology
statement: Let l be prime, s nonnegative, and A a finite ring killed by l^s. For each q, the recorded continuous cohomology functor [def-exc-continuous-cohomology] on discrete continuous modules for the additive group Z_l [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] is naturally isomorphic to H^q(K(-)), where K is the explicit action complex for tau=1 [def-exc-action-two-term-complex].

source.place: Third paragraph, final identification by uniqueness of universal delta-functors

proof.text: Unfold the recorded definition of continuous cohomology to obtain its chosen additive invariant functor V with its natural fixed-submodule equivalences. The degree-zero continuous-cochain theorem provides a finite-limit-preserving invariant functor Vprime. The two fixed-submodule identifications give a natural isomorphism Vprime -> V, so V preserves finite limits as well.

The right derived functors of V form a universal delta-functor R with R^0 naturally isomorphic to V. The cohomology of K forms a delta-functor T. The explicit effacement theorem and the effaceability criterion make T universal; its degree zero is naturally V.

Extend the degree-zero isomorphism R^0 -> T^0 and its inverse by universality. Their composites are morphisms of delta-functors equal in degree zero to the identities; uniqueness makes both composites identities in every degree. Thus their q-components give inverse natural transformations. Rewrite R^q as the recorded right derived invariant functor and T^q as H^q(K(-)).
